thread:
sre-oncall: 👀 alert — apiserver 503/502 spike across eu-west1 and ap-south1, started ~5m ago. Appears correlated with large GPU attach waves from the provisioner. etcd commit latency up and controller-manager leader heartbeats delayed. infra-bot posted alert: /alerts APIServerErrorRate > 5% for 3m

maria: on it, pulling control-plane metrics now

kevin: do we have a diff of the recent provisioner rollout? last change bumped attach parallelism to 30 -> might be overwhelming NAT/conntrack

raj: saw NAT conntrack nearing exhaustion earlier in ap-south; SNAT port reuse high on the NAT gateways. could be that attach RPC fanout is causing TCP churn to apiserver/etcd endpoints.

lucy: can someone paste apiserver logs? I want to confirm `etcdserver: request timed out` vs `connection reset`

sre-oncall: paste from apiserver (redacted):
```
I0303 10:12:01.345 apiserver request.go:123] GET /api/v1/nodes: 503 response from upstream: etcdserver: request timed out
I0303 10:12:02.112 controller-manager queue.go:87] reconcile queue backlog spike: 482 items
etcd: WARN raft: heartbeat missed; avg commit dur 210ms (baseline 6ms)
```

kevin: that commit duration is huge. if etcd leader is overloaded by attach metadata writes we could get apiserver timeouts. is this limited to clusters with gpu-pools?

maria: yes, filtered metrics -> high disk iops on etcd nodes in those regions coincident with attach window. NVMe queue depth ~90%.

raj: also noticed kube-proxy conntrack table per-node is ~65k/65536. SNAT ports realistically exhausted when attach fanout hits control plane + registry pulls from nodes attaching GPUs.

ops-manager: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle provisioner attach concurrency, 2) shift GPU onboarding to staggered windows per-AZ, 3) temporary fallbacks: route new jobs to CPU-only pool or Dedicated nodes. Thoughts?

kevin: agree throttle. can we set `--attach-concurrency=8` for the provisioner and roll? We should avoid a full rollback — prefer rate limit first.

maria: I'll patch a canary on ap-south with concurrency=6 and watch etcd commit latency.

lucy: also recommend enabling prefix KV caching on serving runtime for model metadata writes so the steady-state load on etcd drops. That's medium-term.

raj: short term, we can bump NAT gateway SNAT ports (cloud-side) and increase conntrack on nodes, but both have cost and rollout implications. SNAT bump will add ~$0.7/hr per gateway for our scale in ap-south.

ops-manager: open a ticket for cost impact assessment — tag: #infra-costs and mark P2. Also create incident page and notify Platform PM.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - apiserver/etcd degradation during GPU attach wave — responder: @sre-oncall, link: https://inc.example/INC-2026

maria: canary patch applied in ap-south (deploy/provisioner) at `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/provisioner ATTACH_CONCURRENCY=6`

kevin: rolling it to eu-west now. watching etcd commit histograms and apiserver 5xx rate.

sre-oncall: metrics 2m after patch: etcd p50 commit down 210ms -> 18ms, apiserver 5xx down from 7.1% -> 0.9% in ap-south. Looks promising.

lucy: good sign. After stabilization we should design a capacity plan: gate attach parallelism by NAT headroom, control-plane write QPS, and per-AZ NVMe IO. Add autoscaling signal to provisioner for safe attach rates.

ops-manager: capture action items: [1] Keep throttle in place for 2h, [2] run cost delta for SNAT bump vs longer stagger windows, [3] follow-up RFC for persistent KV cache + attach-scheduling. Assign owners: maria, raj, lucy.

kevin: FYI there was a secondary effect — some controller-manager leader flaps during the peak. controllers recovered after commit latency dropped. need to monitor controller requeue depth.

sre-oncall: closing incident on timeline if metrics stay stable next 30m. Will update incident doc and post summary in #incidents. Nice quick triage team :thumbsup:
